role: developer-authored matched-access development pilot; not held out
prompt: Implement first_slot(calendars: list[list[tuple[int, int]]], duration: int) -> int | None. Each calendar contains a person's AVAILABLE half-open intervals [start, end); intervals can be unsorted, overlapping, touching or repeated. Find the earliest integer t such that [t, t+duration) is entirely available for every person, combining touching and overlapping intervals within each person's calendar. Return None if impossible. If calendars is empty return 0. An empty calendar for any person means impossible. All endpoints are integers from -1000000000 to 1000000000, start < end, duration is a positive integer, and total intervals N <= 100000. Do not mutate the input. Required time O(N log(N+2)) or better; never enumerate time points. Examples: first_slot([[(1,3),(3,6)],[(2,5)]],3)==2; first_slot([[(1,3)],[(3,6)]],1) is None; first_slot([[(-5,0)],[(-3,4)]],2)==-3. Return a complete Python implementation, a correctness explanation and time/space complexity. Use the available Python sandbox to test boundaries and randomized cases. Distinguish observed execution from reasoning. All requirements are supplied; no external research is needed.
